intro: Every state runs its own economic-development incentives on top of federal programs — tax credits, seed funds, deal-closing grants, training reimbursements and more. State incentives stack with federal ones. All 50 states plus DC are covered here, each independently sourced from its official program page; a few flagged programs have sunset or paused for new applicants, and that status is noted where it applies.

states.period: Ongoing, three application periods per year
states.nodalAgency: Governor's Office of Business and Economic Development (GO-Biz)
states.summary: An income tax credit for businesses that want to locate or grow in California, awarded competitively based on jobs created, investment, and strategic importance. FY2025-26 allocation is $215 million statewide.

schemes.name: California Competes Tax Credit
schemes.benefit: Negotiated multi-year income tax credit; $215M allocated statewide for FY2025-26
schemes.description: Competitive tax credit based on a 5-year agreement tied to job-creation, salary, and investment milestones.
schemes.eligibility: Businesses of any size or industry planning to locate, stay, or grow in California

states.summary: Refundable tax credits for firms in targeted industries (finance, tech, manufacturing, agriculture and more) that create jobs or make significant capital investment in New York.

schemes.name: Excelsior Jobs Program
schemes.benefit: Up to 5 refundable tax credits over up to 10 years (jobs, investment, R&D, real property, child care)
schemes.description: Jobs Tax Credit up to 6.85% of wages per net new job; Investment Tax Credit at 2% of qualified investment; R&D credit up to 50% of the federal R&D credit claimed in NY.
schemes.eligibility: Firms in targeted industries creating/maintaining new jobs or making significant investment

states.nodalAgency: Office of the Governor, Economic Development & Tourism
states.summary: The largest state 'deal-closing' fund in the nation, awarding performance-based grants to companies choosing a Texas site over an out-of-state competitor.

schemes.name: Texas Enterprise Fund
schemes.benefit: Negotiated deal-closing grant, sized by an analytical model based on jobs, timeline and wages
schemes.description: Performance-based grant requiring unanimous approval from the Governor, Lieutenant Governor and Speaker of the House, with clawback provisions if job/wage commitments aren't met.
schemes.eligibility: Well-established, financially sound businesses in advanced industries with a competing out-of-state site

states.policy: MassVentures START Program & Early Stage Fund
states.summary: Non-dilutive funding for Massachusetts companies commercializing SBIR/STTR Phase II technology, plus direct seed-stage equity investment.

schemes.name: START Program
schemes.benefit: $100,000-$500,000 non-dilutive funding
schemes.description: For companies that have received a federal SBIR/STTR Phase II award; covers commercialization activities not funded by the federal grant. $41.7M awarded to 141 companies since 2012.
schemes.eligibility: Massachusetts-based companies with a Phase II SBIR/STTR award

schemes.name: Early Stage Fund
schemes.benefit: $250,000-$500,000 initial Series A investment
schemes.description: Direct equity investment in Massachusetts seed-stage deep-tech companies, with potential for follow-on funding.
schemes.eligibility: Massachusetts-based seed-stage technology companies

states.nodalAgency: PA Department of Community & Economic Development (via the Ben Franklin Technology Development Authority)
states.summary: Pennsylvania's statewide innovation network providing early-stage funding and hands-on support through four regional partner organizations.

schemes.name: Ben Franklin Technology Partners funding
schemes.benefit: Up to $500,000 for tech startups (series of investments); up to $250,000 for existing manufacturers
schemes.description: Early-stage investment plus expert guidance and strategic partnerships, delivered through regional Ben Franklin offices covering the whole state.
schemes.eligibility: Pennsylvania-based startups and manufacturers

states.summary: Non-dilutive seed grants for early-stage North Carolina startups with a proven concept, running since 2006.

schemes.name: NC IDEA SEED Grant
schemes.benefit: $50,000 non-dilutive grant
schemes.description: Milestone-based grant over 6-12 months for startups with a demonstrated proof of concept and MVP; over $10.3M awarded to 225+ companies since 2006.
schemes.eligibility: At least one full-time founder living in North Carolina; proven concept, not yet profitable

states.summary: Maryland's leading source of funding for early-stage, technology-based businesses, with a portfolio of 400+ seed investments since 1998.

schemes.name: TEDCO Seed Investment Fund
schemes.benefit: Seed-stage investment; amount varies by deal
schemes.description: Targets Maryland companies with fewer than 20 employees, generally under 5 years old, developing and commercializing new technology-based products.
schemes.eligibility: Maryland principal place of business; at least one full-time employee

states.nodalAgency: Michigan Strategic Fund / Michigan Economic Development Corporation (MEDC)
states.summary: Performance-based grants (with some loan/other-support options) for businesses creating jobs or making qualified investment in Michigan.

schemes.name: Michigan Business Development Program
schemes.benefit: Negotiated performance-based grant with flexible terms; may include repayment provisions
schemes.description: Preference given to businesses choosing to locate or expand in Michigan over an out-of-state alternative.
schemes.eligibility: Businesses creating qualified new jobs and/or making qualified new investment in Michigan

states.nodalAgency: Governor's Office of Workforce Transformation / Ohio Department of Development
states.summary: Reimburses Ohio employers for the cost of short-term, technology-focused credentials for current and future employees.

schemes.name: TechCred
schemes.benefit: Up to $1,000 per employee per credential, max $30,000 per application period
schemes.description: Reimburses training costs for short-term, industry-recognized, tech-focused credentials (IT, cybersecurity, robotics/automation, and more) completed within a year.
schemes.eligibility: Ohio employers, using a training provider from the state's eligible-provider list

states.period: Annual application cycles (e.g. Proof of Concept due Aug 27, 2026)
states.nodalAgency: Colorado Office of Economic Development & International Trade (OEDIT)
states.summary: State grants supporting Colorado's advanced-industry startups and research institutions across four grant tracks.

schemes.name: Advanced Industries Proof of Concept Grant
schemes.description: Helps Colorado research institutions speed up applied research and commercialize it with private-sector partners.
schemes.eligibility: Colorado research institutions and their commercialization partners

schemes.name: Advanced Industries Early-Stage Capital and Retention Grant
schemes.description: Helps Colorado-based advanced-industries companies develop and commercialize technologies created or manufactured in-state.
schemes.eligibility: Colorado-based advanced-industries technology businesses

states.policy: Virginia Innovation Partnership Corporation (VIPC) funding programs
states.nodalAgency: Virginia Innovation Partnership Corporation (nonprofit arm of VIPA)
states.summary: Virginia's commercialization and seed-stage economic-development driver, running multiple grant and direct-investment programs for early-stage companies.

schemes.name: Launch Program
schemes.benefit: Non-dilutive grants and dilutive convertible notes
schemes.description: For high-potential, pre-MVP Virginia startups that have raised minimal equity and generated limited revenue.
schemes.eligibility: Pre-MVP Virginia startups with strong potential economic impact

schemes.name: Lab-to-Launch Initiative
schemes.description: For early-stage Virginia startups using a Fast-Track License Agreement with one of Virginia's six R1-designated universities.
schemes.eligibility: Virginia-based startups licensing university technology

schemes.name: Virginia Venture Partners (VVP)
schemes.benefit: $250,000 pre-seed; up to $1M seed-stage
schemes.description: VIPC's direct venture-capital investment platform for high-potential Virginia-based startups.
schemes.eligibility: Virginia-based startups with high growth potential

states.policy: Invest Georgia / Georgia Venture Capital Program
states.nodalAgency: Invest Georgia (state instrumentality) / Georgia Department of Community Affairs
states.summary: A state-backed fund-of-funds that invests as a limited partner in seed, venture-capital, and growth-equity funds targeting Georgia-based businesses.

schemes.name: Georgia Venture Capital Program
schemes.benefit: $30M SSBCI allocation deployed via participating VC funds
schemes.description: Invest Georgia invests as a limited partner in seed and early-stage VC funds, including funds targeting SEDI-owned businesses, which in turn invest in Georgia startups.
schemes.eligibility: Georgia-based businesses funded indirectly through participating venture-capital funds

states.summary: Discretionary jobs and investment tax credits for companies creating jobs and capital investment in Alabama.

schemes.name: Alabama Jobs Act — Jobs Credit
schemes.benefit: Cash rebate up to 3% of gross payroll, up to 10 years
schemes.description: Discretionary incentive granted by the Secretary of Commerce and approved by the Governor for eligible Alabama employees.
schemes.eligibility: Qualifying projects approved under the Alabama Jobs Act

schemes.name: Alabama Jobs Act — Investment Credit
schemes.benefit: Up to 1.5% annually on qualified capital investment, up to 10 years
schemes.description: Tax credit against state tax liabilities, carried forward up to 5 years.
schemes.eligibility: Qualifying capital investment projects

states.summary: A refundable tax credit for manufacturing, R&D, or headquarters facilities that create net new jobs in Arizona.

schemes.name: Qualified Facility Tax Credit
schemes.benefit: Lesser of 10% of investment or $20,000-$30,000 per net new job, up to $30M/year per taxpayer
schemes.description: Refundable income tax credit claimed in 5 equal installments, authorized through December 2030 on a first-come, first-served basis.
schemes.eligibility: Minimum capital investment, net new jobs at required wage thresholds, mostly out-of-state sales, employee health coverage

states.summary: Discretionary income-tax credits and payroll rebates for new or expanding Arkansas businesses.

schemes.name: ArkPlus
schemes.benefit: Up to 10% of total project investment as an income tax credit
schemes.description: Discretionary credit requiring minimum investment and new full-time payroll, tier-dependent.
schemes.eligibility: Minimum investment and new full-time permanent payroll depending on county tier

schemes.name: Create Rebate
schemes.benefit: 3.9%-5% annual cash payment on new payroll, up to 10 years
schemes.description: Requires minimum $2M new payroll within 24 months of the incentive agreement.
schemes.eligibility: Minimum new full-time permanent payroll, discretionary approval by AEDC director

states.nodalAgency: CT Department of Economic and Community Development (DECD)
states.summary: A refundable tax rebate for companies in targeted industries that grow their Connecticut workforce.

schemes.name: JobsCT Tax Rebate
schemes.benefit: 25% rebate on new-employee withholding taxes (50% in Distressed Municipalities/Opportunity Zones)
schemes.description: Requires a minimum of 25 new full-time jobs at $37,500+ wage; rebate starts 24 months after DECD approval.
schemes.eligibility: Targeted industries; minimum 25 new FTEs meeting wage threshold

states.summary: Delaware's primary discretionary fund for business expansion, retention, and relocation, plus STEM-focused EDGE grants.

schemes.name: Delaware Strategic Fund
schemes.benefit: Negotiated low-interest loans or grants
schemes.description: Discretionary financial assistance for job creation, expansion, relocation, and brownfield redevelopment.
schemes.eligibility: Businesses creating jobs at sustainable wages; negotiated case-by-case

schemes.name: EDGE Grants
schemes.benefit: Up to $100,000 (STEM) or $50,000 (non-STEM entrepreneur class)
schemes.description: Grants for eligible expenses of early-stage Delaware companies.
schemes.eligibility: Early-stage Delaware companies, STEM or entrepreneur class

states.summary: State grants for public infrastructure and workforce training that support targeted-industry economic development (Florida's former direct-refund QTI program was repealed in 2023).

schemes.name: Florida Job Growth Grant Fund
schemes.benefit: Project-based; over $318M awarded since 2019
schemes.description: Funds public infrastructure and workforce training proposals chosen by the Governor's office — an indirect benefit to area businesses rather than a direct-to-company grant.
schemes.eligibility: Public entities and communities proposing infrastructure or workforce-training projects

states.summary: A performance-based tax credit on new state revenue generated by companies expanding in or relocating to Idaho.

schemes.name: Tax Reimbursement Incentive
schemes.benefit: Up to 30% credit on income, payroll and sales taxes, up to 15 years
schemes.description: Negotiated award based on job quality/quantity and economic impact; open to new and expanding Idaho businesses.
schemes.eligibility: New full-time jobs at or above county average wage

states.nodalAgency: Illinois Department of Commerce and Economic Opportunity (DCEO)
states.summary: Illinois's foundational tax-credit program for job creation, retention, and capital investment, extended through June 2027.

schemes.name: Economic Development for a Growing Economy (EDGE)
schemes.benefit: 50-75% of new-job withholding as non-refundable income tax credit, up to 10 years
schemes.description: Higher rate (75%) for jobs created in underserved areas.
schemes.eligibility: Businesses creating/retaining full-time jobs and making capital investment in Illinois

schemes.name: EDGE for Startups
schemes.benefit: Tailored EDGE terms for early-stage companies
schemes.description: A startup-specific track of the EDGE program.
schemes.eligibility: Illinois-based early-stage companies

states.policy: Economic Development for a Growing Economy (EDGE)
states.summary: Indiana's primary discretionary job-creation tax credit, refundable and certified annually.

schemes.name: EDGE Tax Credit
schemes.benefit: Refundable credit up to 100% of incremental withholding, up to 20 years
schemes.description: Performance-based; certified annually by IEDC pursuant to an EDGE Agreement.
schemes.eligibility: Companies committing to net new jobs and capital investment in Indiana

states.policy: High Quality Jobs Program (transitioning to Business Incentives for Growth)
states.summary: Iowa's flagship business-assistance package of tax credits, exemptions and refunds — being replaced by the Business Incentives for Growth (BIG) Program; verify current status before applying.

schemes.name: High Quality Jobs (HQJ) Program
schemes.benefit: Investment tax credits, sales/use tax refunds, R&D activities credit
schemes.description: Flexible award package for non-retail/non-service businesses meeting wage requirements; being succeeded by the BIG Program.
schemes.eligibility: Non-retail/non-service business meeting wage thresholds

states.summary: A payroll-withholding retention incentive for companies creating jobs in Kansas.

schemes.name: PEAK
schemes.benefit: Refund of up to 95% of new-employee payroll withholding, up to 7-10 years
schemes.description: 10 new metro jobs (5 non-metro) within 2 years for 7 years of benefit; 100 new jobs unlocks 10 years.
schemes.eligibility: For-profit or qualifying nonprofit; county median wage and health-coverage requirements

states.summary: A tax-credit and wage-assessment incentive for manufacturing, technology, and headquarters projects.

schemes.name: Kentucky Business Investment Program
schemes.benefit: Credit up to 100% of state income tax liability plus 5% wage assessment, up to 15 years
schemes.description: Requires minimum 10 new full-time jobs and $100,000 in eligible costs.
schemes.eligibility: Manufacturing, agribusiness, non-retail service/technology, or HQ operations

states.summary: A cash-rebate program for targeted-industry companies creating quality jobs in Louisiana.

schemes.name: Quality Jobs Rebate
schemes.benefit: 4-6% annual payroll rebate, up to 10 years, plus a sales/use or facility-expense rebate
schemes.description: Targets bioscience, manufacturing, software, clean energy, food technology, and other named industries.
schemes.eligibility: Minimum new direct jobs/payroll (scaled by company size) at a minimum wage threshold

states.policy: Pine Tree Development Zone (closed to new applicants Dec 31, 2024)
states.nodalAgency: Maine Department of Economic and Community Development
states.summary: Maine's flagship tax-reduction zone program for qualified sectors — no longer accepting new applicants; listed for reference while Maine's replacement incentive framework is finalized.

schemes.name: Pine Tree Development Zone (legacy)
schemes.benefit: Up to 100% corporate tax credit (years 1-5), 50% (years 6-10), plus sales/use tax exemptions
schemes.description: Existing participants continue to receive benefits; the program closed to new applications December 31, 2024.
schemes.eligibility: Historic — check Maine DECD for the current replacement incentive

states.nodalAgency: Minnesota Department of Employment and Economic Development (DEED)
states.summary: A pay-for-performance award for companies meeting job-creation and capital-investment targets.

schemes.name: Job Creation Fund
schemes.benefit: $1,000-$5,000 per job/year, up to $1M-$2M total, plus up to 7.5% real-property rebate
schemes.description: Requires minimum investment ($500K, or $250K for Targeted Populations) and new FTEs within set timeframes.
schemes.eligibility: Manufacturing, warehouse/distribution, IT, finance, insurance, or professional/technical services

states.summary: A cash-rebate program for qualified employers creating quality jobs in Mississippi.

schemes.name: Advantage Jobs Incentive Program
schemes.benefit: Rebate up to 90% of withheld state income taxes, up to 10 years
schemes.description: Requires minimum new jobs (10-25 depending on county tier) at 125% of county/state average wage.
schemes.eligibility: Non-retail, non-gaming businesses meeting wage and job-count thresholds

states.summary: Missouri's flagship job-creation incentive with tiers scaled to company size, from small Zone Works projects to Mega Works.

schemes.name: Missouri Works
schemes.benefit: 100% state withholding retention and/or refundable tax credits; $10M annual program cap
schemes.description: Tiers: Zone/Rural Works (2 jobs), Statewide Works (10 jobs), Mega Works (100 jobs); $5M of the cap reserved for minority/women/small businesses.
schemes.eligibility: New jobs at required wage thresholds by tier

states.policy: Big Sky Economic Development Trust Fund (currently not accepting applications)
states.summary: State-funded grants for job-creation and planning projects, funded by coal severance tax revenue — currently paused for new applications.

schemes.name: Big Sky Economic Development Trust Fund
schemes.benefit: Project-based job-creation and planning grants
schemes.description: 75% of funding goes to job-creation projects, 25% to planning; check current application status before relying on this program.
schemes.eligibility: Montana economic-development job-creation or planning projects

states.summary: Nebraska's current-generation tax incentive package, replacing the Nebraska Advantage Act as of January 2021.

schemes.name: ImagiNE Nebraska Act
schemes.benefit: 4-7% investment credits, 4-9% wage credits, plus sales/use tax refunds
schemes.description: Based on job creation and investment levels; as of late 2024, 50 companies had pledged 2,481 jobs and $1.55B investment under the Act.
schemes.eligibility: Businesses expanding or relocating to Nebraska meeting investment/job thresholds

states.summary: Five discretionary tax-abatement programs administered by GOED to attract or grow Nevada businesses.

schemes.name: Standard & Data Center Tax Abatements
schemes.benefit: Sales/use, payroll (Modified Business Tax), and personal property tax abatements — data centers as low as 2% for 10-20 years
schemes.description: Applications go through a Regional Development Authority to GOED.
schemes.eligibility: Businesses meeting GOED capital-investment and job thresholds

states.nodalAgency: NH Department of Business and Economic Affairs
states.summary: A matching workforce-training grant for New Hampshire businesses.

schemes.name: Job Training Fund / WorkInvestNH
schemes.benefit: $750-$100,000 matching grant for skills training
schemes.description: Employer must match the award; funds training costs only, not wages.
schemes.eligibility: NH businesses paying into the NH Unemployment Trust Fund

states.summary: A per-job tax credit under the 2020 Economic Recovery Act for priority-sector projects and targeted communities.

schemes.name: Emerge Program
schemes.benefit: $500-$8,000 per job tax credit, up to 7 years
schemes.description: Requires 35+ new full-time jobs (lower for small business/targeted industries) and 80% NJ work-time/withholding.
schemes.eligibility: Eligible incentive location; minimum capital investment; competitive out-of-state alternative shown

states.summary: State grants to local governments to fund infrastructure supporting expanding or relocating businesses.

schemes.name: LEDA
schemes.benefit: Reimbursement-basis grants for land, buildings, and infrastructure
schemes.description: Grants flow to local governments (municipality/county), not directly to companies; extra weight given to rural/underserved projects.
schemes.eligibility: Company must manufacture in NM or provide a non-retail service with 50%+ revenue from outside NM

states.summary: Flexible state financing including a deal-closing loan program and an angel-investment match.

schemes.name: Advance ND
schemes.benefit: Low-interest loans up to $20,000,000 at 2%
schemes.description: Deal-closing loans for new industrial projects adding capital investment, resource value, and jobs.
schemes.eligibility: New industrial projects in North Dakota

schemes.name: Angel Match Program
schemes.benefit: State match of qualifying angel investments
schemes.description: Increases available capital for North Dakota businesses.
schemes.eligibility: North Dakota businesses receiving qualifying angel investment

states.summary: A quarterly payroll rebate for qualifying companies, with variants for small employers and knowledge-based industries.

schemes.name: Quality Jobs Program
schemes.benefit: Up to 5% of new payroll quarterly, up to 10 years
schemes.description: Requires $2.5M+ new payroll investment (lower for targeted industries) and wage/health-insurance requirements.
schemes.eligibility: Manufacturers and other qualifying industries meeting payroll thresholds

schemes.name: 21st Century Quality Jobs Program
schemes.benefit: Up to 10% of new payroll, up to 10 years
schemes.description: For knowledge-based, highly-skilled workforce industries; 10 jobs at high average wage thresholds.
schemes.eligibility: Knowledge-based industries meeting wage requirements

states.summary: A revolving gap-financing loan fund for Oregon traded-sector businesses.

schemes.name: Oregon Business Development Fund
schemes.benefit: Fixed-rate gap loans up to $2,000,000, terms up to 20 years
schemes.description: Used alongside a traditional lender; preference for rural/distressed areas and small businesses under 100 employees.
schemes.eligibility: Traded-sector businesses (manufacturing, processing, distribution) creating/retaining jobs

states.summary: Rhode Island's job-creation tax credit — its statutory sunset date has passed; check Commerce RI for its current successor program.

schemes.name: Qualified Jobs Incentive (legacy)
schemes.benefit: $2,500-$7,500 per new full-time job per year, up to 10 years
schemes.description: Credit roughly matched W-2 withholding, capped at 75% of that withholding for post-2019 approvals; unused credit carries forward 4 years.
schemes.eligibility: Historic — verify current Commerce RI incentive offerings

states.summary: A statutory corporate income tax credit for new and expanding businesses creating jobs.

schemes.name: Job Tax Credit (JTC)
schemes.benefit: $1,500-$9,000 per job/year, offsetting up to 50% of corporate income tax
schemes.description: Requires average monthly increase of 10 new full-time jobs; higher credit in multi-county industrial parks or Brownfields sites; carries forward up to 15 years.
schemes.eligibility: Corporations, sole proprietors, partnerships, S-corps, and LLCs creating qualifying jobs

states.nodalAgency: South Dakota Governor's Office of Economic Development (GOED)
states.summary: South Dakota's flagship low-interest revolving loan fund for job-growth projects.

schemes.name: Revolving Economic Development & Initiative (REDI) Fund
schemes.benefit: Low-interest loans (currently 3%) up to 45% of project cost
schemes.description: Requires 10% minimum equity contribution and a shared first-lien position on financed assets; open to start-ups and expanding/relocating businesses.
schemes.eligibility: Start-up, expanding, or relocating South Dakota businesses and local development corporations

states.nodalAgency: Tennessee Department of Economic and Community Development (ECD)
states.summary: A three-part discretionary grant program supporting job training, infrastructure, and exceptional economic-development projects.

schemes.name: FastTrack Job Training Assistance
schemes.benefit: Negotiated grants for training net new full-time employees
schemes.description: Provided directly to new or expanding companies for employee training costs.
schemes.eligibility: New or expanding Tennessee companies, negotiated case-by-case

schemes.name: FastTrack Infrastructure Development
schemes.benefit: Grants to communities reimbursing eligible company expenditures
schemes.description: Covers real property acquisition, new construction, and building retrofit for expanding/relocating companies.
schemes.eligibility: Local communities supporting a qualifying company project

states.summary: A post-performance refundable tax credit for high-wage job creation, with a rural variant (REDTIF).

schemes.name: EDTIF
schemes.benefit: Up to 30% of new state revenues (sales, corporate, withholding) over 5-10 years
schemes.description: Post-performance credit after the company meets capital-investment and job-creation obligations; wages must be 110% of average county wage.
schemes.eligibility: Advanced manufacturing, aerospace/defense, financial services, life sciences, healthcare, software, IT

states.summary: A performance-based cash incentive tied to the incremental state tax revenue a project generates.

schemes.name: VEGI
schemes.benefit: Cash incentive proportional to incremental state tax revenue generated
schemes.description: Paid only after annual performance requirements (jobs, payroll, capital investment) are met and maintained — no upfront payment.
schemes.eligibility: Growth beyond a business's organic trajectory, approved by VEPC

states.summary: A set of Business & Occupation (B&O) tax credits, deferrals, and exemptions rather than a single flagship program.

schemes.name: High Technology B&O Tax Credit
schemes.benefit: Credit against B&O tax for qualifying R&D spending
schemes.description: One of several targeted B&O credits (alongside Rural County, Small Business, and veteran-hiring credits).
schemes.eligibility: Washington businesses conducting qualifying R&D or other targeted activity

schemes.name: Sales/Use Tax Exemption — Manufacturing & R&D Equipment
schemes.benefit: Exemption on qualifying machinery and equipment
schemes.description: For equipment used directly in manufacturing or R&D operations.
schemes.eligibility: Washington manufacturing or R&D operations

states.nodalAgency: West Virginia Department of Economic Development
states.summary: A family of tax credits for job creation, manufacturing investment, and headquarters relocation.

schemes.name: Economic Opportunity Tax Credit
schemes.benefit: Offsets up to 80% of specified business taxes, up to 13 years
schemes.description: Requires at least 20 new jobs (10 for qualified small business) within specified time limits.
schemes.eligibility: Qualified companies creating new jobs via business expansion

schemes.name: High Wage Growth Tax Credit
schemes.benefit: Payroll incentive for new high-wage jobs
schemes.description: For businesses creating 10 or more new high-paying jobs.
schemes.eligibility: West Virginia businesses adding qualifying high-wage positions

states.summary: Refundable tax credits for job creation, capital investment, training, and headquarters retention.

schemes.name: Business Development Tax Credit
schemes.benefit: Refundable credits; WEDC may allocate up to $22M/year
schemes.description: Minimum $250,000 capital investment as of 2024; can include workforce-housing and child-care incentives.
schemes.eligibility: Businesses in or relocating to Wisconsin maintaining or growing net employment

states.policy: Building Resilient Communities (formerly Business Ready Community)
states.summary: State grants and loans to communities for public infrastructure supporting business location or expansion.

schemes.name: Building Resilient Communities Grant & Loan
schemes.benefit: Typical maximum award $3M; data-center track up to $2.25M
schemes.description: Funds go to cities/towns/counties for infrastructure tied to a committed business project, not directly to companies.
schemes.eligibility: Wyoming communities with a business commitment to locate or expand

states.nodalAgency: Alaska Dept. of Commerce, Community & Economic Development (Division of Economic Development)
states.summary: State direct-lending and R&D tax credit programs supporting new and expanding Alaska businesses.

schemes.name: New Business Incentive Program
schemes.benefit: Economic development grant for new manufacturing/value-added businesses
schemes.description: Targets substantial businesses creating high-value, year-round jobs in Alaska.
schemes.eligibility: New or expanding manufacturing/value-added businesses in Alaska

schemes.name: Alaska R&D Tax Credit
schemes.benefit: Dollar-for-dollar offset against corporate net income tax
schemes.description: Designed to encourage innovation spending by Alaska businesses.
schemes.eligibility: Alaska businesses with qualifying R&D expenditures

states.summary: Hawaii's current R&D tax credit for qualified high-tech research, replacing the earlier (repealed) Act 221 high-tech investment credit.

schemes.name: Tax Credit for Research Activities
schemes.benefit: Refundable credit against qualified research expenses; $5M annual statewide cap
schemes.description: The cap has been reached almost immediately in each recent year — apply as soon as the window opens.
schemes.eligibility: Hawaii businesses conducting 50%+ of activity in qualified research

states.nodalAgency: DC Office of Tax and Revenue / Dept. of Housing and Enterprise Development
states.summary: DC's flagship tax-incentive package for technology companies operating in the District.

schemes.name: QHTC Tax Benefits
schemes.benefit: 3% reduced capital gains rate; up to $15,000/employee wage-tax credit; 5-year property tax freeze on office improvements
schemes.description: Requires 51%+ DC-sourced revenue from qualifying high-tech activity and 10+ qualified DC employees.
schemes.eligibility: For-profit DC-based high-tech company outside the Ballpark TIF Area
